title: Quarterly runway: Hosted service rollout tranches and model curation playbook
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Goal: Define a clear, testable quarterly runway for the Hosted API product line that pairs model catalog pruning/curation with staggered rollout tranches (canary -> regional -> global) and explicit cost/performance scenarios. This ticket captures the playbook we will use to: 1) choose which model variants are eligible for hosted tiers this quarter, 2) define rollout tranches and acceptance gates (latency/99th, cost per 1k tokens, quality regressions on core evals), and 3) create a run-book for cross-team execution (RTC with Eng, Console, SRE, Sales).

Scope (in-scope): model selection criteria (accuracy vs cost buckets), tranche definitions and SLO gates, rollback and fallback mapping to compatible variants, success metrics for OKR alignment, and CI/eval artifacts to validate quality prior to each tranche. Out-of-scope: heavy re-architecture of runtime, new GPU procurement, or long-term Dedicated capacity contracts (handled by separate Dedicated runway tickets).

Deliverables: 
- Final model eligibility matrix (model, quantization profile, inference latency 95/99, cost bucket) for hosted tiers.
- Tranche schedule and gating checklist (canary -> region -> global) with owners and automated checks.
- Quality/eval suite for regression detection (prompt sets, pass/fail thresholds per intent class).
- Cost sensitivity scenarios showing token-unit cost at 1x, 2x, and 5x traffic with/without prefix cache and batching.
- Rollout playbook (step-by-step) including signal dashboards and rollback thresholds, plus links to PRs and runbooks.

Success metrics (tie to OKRs): 
- Reduce hosted API average cost-per-1k-tokens by 12% for standard text generation workloads by end of cycle (OKR: Cost Efficiency).
- Maintain 99th-percentile latency SLO within +10% of baseline for 95% of rollouts (OKR: Reliability).
- Zero production-quality regressions detected by automatic eval suite in 3/3 tranche rollouts (OKR: Quality).

Key stakeholders: PM (Sofia Martinez), Eng owners (Liam Chen, Priya Rao), Runtime lead (Marcus Elliot), Console & Observability (Taylor Nguyen), SRE (Aisha Kapoor), Sales (Ruben Ortega) for customer communication.

Decision drivers and trade-offs considered: 
- We will prefer smaller model variants for cost buckets where expected quality delta < 3% on our core evals. The break-even calculus includes predicted token mix (embeddings vs generation), average request length, and prefix reuse rate.
- Batching aggressiveness will be conservative during regional canaries; queueing time budgets defined per tranche to avoid latency SLO violations.
- Fallback mapping: each primary model must have a compatible fallback model (same tokenizer/response shape) with documented behavior under overload.

Artifacts & links: 
- Confluence planning doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PM/pages/Hosted+Service+Runway+Q2 (draft)
- Drive: https://drive.google.com/hosted-runway/q2-model-matrix (model matrices & cost sheets)
- Eval harness PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/evals/pull/482
- Canary automation infra PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/deployments/pull/901

Risks & mitigations: 
- Risk: Unexpected quality regressions in long-tail prompts. Mitigation: Expand eval suite with 200 long-tail prompts from customer shadowing and hold a manual review gate for canary.
- Risk: Cost projections optimistic if prefix reuse lower than assumed. Mitigation: Run a 7-day shadow traffic simulation on staging and adjust batching/cache knobs before region rollout.
- Risk: Cross-team coordination friction (Console dashboards + SRE alerts). Mitigation: Pre-schedule a 2-week runbook dry-run and include pre-built dashboard templates in the playbook.

Next steps (first 2 weeks): 
1) Complete the model eligibility matrix and tag owners (Due: 2025-02-20).
2) Finalize tranche gating checklist and create Playbook PR (Due: 2025-02-28).
3) Run 7-day traffic shadow with proposed batching/cache settings (Start: 2025-03-03).
